## monolibdata1e absorb → CStopwatchUtil (Wii/1.1, data MATCH)

- Symptom:   last monolib catch-all blob (`src/monolibdata1e.cpp`, Matching
  `retail_data`) held a single 0x280 `.bss` symbol `lbl_eu_80657238` while
  `CStopwatchUtil.cpp` only `extern`'d it; goal is absorb into the owning TU
  so the blob can leave `configure.py`.
- Cause:     MWCC treats bare `extern "C" T name[N];` (no braces / no
  initializer) as a **declaration** → ELF `SHN_UNDEF`, no `.bss`. The braced
  form `extern "C" { T name[N]; }` (or `= {}`) emits the definition. Nested
  `CStopwatchUtil::StopwatchEntry` works inside the braces.
- Fix:       define `extern "C" { CStopwatchUtil::StopwatchEntry lbl_eu_80657238[16]; }`
  in `libs/monolib/src/util/CStopwatchUtil.cpp`; move
  `.bss start:0x80657238 end:0x806574B8` onto that unit in `config/us/splits.txt`;
  remove `Object(Matching, "monolibdata1e.cpp")` from `configure.py` and delete
  `src/monolibdata1e.cpp`. Keep existing `UNIT_RULES` `.sdata2` pool drop.
- Result:    `data diff main/monolib/src/util/CStopwatchUtil` → `VERDICT: MATCH`
  (`.bss` 0x280 align 8); `.text` size still 0x2F8 exact vs retail.
- Applies to/a.k.a.: any absorb that turns a soft-extern into a TU-local
  definition under MWCC — always use braced `extern "C" { ... }` or an
  initializer; verify with elftools that the symbol is DEFINED before trusting
  `data diff` (stale `.o` / missing ninja rebuild will lie).

## CfGimmick .sdata2 struct-pool -> individual SDA labels (Wii/1.1, +6 FULL, split FAIL->PASS)
- Symptom:   CfGimmick_ApplyPartyMoveSpeed/A1DC at 8.2% with 0xb8->0xc4 frames (+1 saved GPR each);
  decomp `li r31,0 + lfs f1,8(r31)` (absolute) vs retail `lfs f1,0(r0)` (SDA21);
  relocs drifted `sdata2num_CfGimmick -> lbl_eu_80668350/358`. UVF70 call spelling
  (`player->CfObject_UnkVirtualFunc70(float)`, slot +0x168) was already correct.
- Cause:     all .sdata2 numbers lived in ONE 0x30-byte struct, which exceeds MWCC's
  small-data threshold, so every member access materialized an absolute address in
  a dedicated GPR (stolen loop-counter register -> extra save, +0x10 frame each).
  Prior waves proved the syncModelRate inline forwarder also grows frames - the
  frame cost was addressing, not call spelling.
- Fix:       six floats as individual `extern "C"` `.sdata2` labels (SDA-eligible,
  SDA21 via r0, no extra GPR); tail doubles KEPT in a 16-byte struct (individual
  2^52 literal gets deduped into the codegen int->float pool, dropping its slot
  and pulling the 68378 pair up to 0x50); 68378 as `f32[2]` (retail sz8) with the
  header decl widened scalar->[2] and two `[0]` use sites (no other TU uses it).
  MWCC `extern "C"` must wrap declspec lines in a block (trailing `extern "C"`
  is a 10121 syntax error on 1.1).
- Result:    28/51 -> 34/51 FULL (A124/A1DC 100% at exact 0xb8, plus 8C48/8C60/
  915C/9754), split FAIL +0x24 -> PASS (0x24 spare), .sdata2 first 0x60 bytes
  now byte-identical to retail obj. Remainder: TU-local `@N` pool-name drift on
  the SDA21 relocs (MWCC folds const-label loads into its literal pool; code
  bytes identical) - witness-certifiable per PATTERNS pool-cookie rule, not pads.
- Applies to/a.k.a.: any TU pooling .sdata2 numbers in a struct (frame growth +
  reloc drift); tail-struct guard for dedup-prone magic doubles; cf. PATTERNS
  1b/1d/1k/7i pool rules.

## CActorParam alias->virtual promotion: inline-alias dispatch-order flip (Wii/1.1, FULL kept)
- Symptom:   promoting the `CActorParam_getSpentCurrency` inline alias to the
  call site (`getLevelExp() - getSpentCurrency()` replacing
  `getLevelExp() - UnkVirtualFunc85()`) dropped UnkVirtualFunc86 100% -> 87%
  (3 reg_swap: vtable offsets 496/488 swapped, subf operands flipped).
- Cause:     the alias adds one inline frame around the second virtual
  dispatch; MWCC then schedules the two vtable calls in the opposite order
  (alias's dispatch first). Same class of ordering hazard as expression-order
  residuals: the call TEXT changed, so the scheduler chose differently.
- Fix:       named locals pin the order (`u32 a = getLevelExp(); u32 b =
  getSpentCurrency(); return a - b;`) -> 100% again. Lesson: when replacing
  a direct virtual call with an alias (or vice versa) inside a multi-call
  expression, expect dispatch-order flips and pin with locals. (External TUs
  calling an alias need NO change: alias->virtual resolution with unchanged
  call text is codegen-neutral - proven by CfObjectPc syncArtsEntry staying
  FULL and CtrlObjectParam CtrlObjectParam_ActivateActorOwner showing only its pre-existing
  mParam offset drift.)
- Result:    UnkVirtualFunc86 FULL_MATCH under the alias spelling; pattern
  reused for 18 CActorParam slot promotions (decl + def + CREvtModel
  hand-vtable + symbols.txt us/jp/eu + targets.json id-preserving rename),
  unit holds 44/60 FULL, split PASS.

## CChain_TickChain / kyoshin/cf/chain/CChain — case-6 unk0 reloads + scratch store order → local alignment (Wii/1.1 -O4, ~36% near-miss)

- Fix:       keep actor live; reload `actor->unk0` at each later call/store; write scratch as D, 12, float, 10, 6
- Result:    case 5 scratch + case 6 body instruction-match; function still ~36.5% (639 structural) / 0x12bc vs 0x12c8. Residual: case 5 `lbz field_2` vs `lfs` schedule, switch `cmpli 26` vs `25`, member-wrap colors, later cascade

## CChain_TickChain / kyoshin/cf/chain/CChain — empty case 0x1a folds jumptable bound (Wii/1.1 -O4, 38.4% near-miss)
- Symptom:   `cmpli r5, 25` vs retail `cmpli r5, 26`; 12 then 8 bytes short; case 5 tail `lfs` before `lbz field_2`

- Result:    38.4% (623 structural / 117 reg_swap) / 0x12c0 vs 0x12c8. Next: serialize case 5 `lbz`/`lfs` without TU-wide schedule off; keep wrap `extsb` + count `lwz`/`extsh` live

## CChain_TickChain / kyoshin/cf/chain/CChain — size-parity wrap; witness dies on case 5 lfs hoist (Wii/1.1 -O4, 40.1% / objdiff 97.5%)
- Symptom:   cycle `witness-gate: mnemonic | slot 358: lbz vs lfs`; hexdiff 40.1% at exact 0x12c8; u8 wrap with both `(u8)(idx±1)` is 56.3% but 1205 vs 1202 insns

## CChain_TickChain / kyoshin/cf/chain/CChain — O4 will not un-hoist case 5 lfs via local pragmas (40.1%, size exact)
- Symptom:   after `bl aiAppendToRing`, decomp `lfs` then `li 1` then `lbz field_2`; retail `lbz` then `li 1` then `lfs`

## CChain_TickChain / kyoshin/cf/chain/CChain — case 5 SDA21 lfs is independent; extra next-store un-hoists (Wii/1.1 -O4)
- Symptom:   retail tail after `bl aiAppendToRing` is `lbz; li 1; lfs; li 60; addi; stfs; …` (SDA21 `lfs` of `lbl_eu_80668A44`). Checkpoint 40.1% emits `lfs` first
- Cause:     retail `lfs` is `R_PPC_EMB_SDA21` — no GPR data edge from `field_2`. Folding indexes / `lfsx` change the encoding. Same-value rewrite of `field_2` is DCE'd. Mid-fn `optimize_for_size` is ignored. A second `addi` successor (store `next` to scratch `field_6`) raises `lbz` enough that the scheduler emits the retail prefix through `addi`
- Fix:       case 0xc decrement `idx -= 1` (buy 4B); after the call `u8 next = state+1; scratchB.mFields.field_6 = next` then timer stores; `case 0x1a: return`
- Result:    size `0x12c8` exact; hexdiff structural ~756 (wrap buy). Tail: `lbz; li 1; lfs; li 60; addi; stb field_6; stfs; …`. Witness should die at slot 363 `stb` vs `stfs`. Next: issue `stfs` immediately after `addi` without losing the 5-insn prefix (or sink the extra `stb` with no net insn)
- Evidence:  us-80279fbc / src/kyoshin/cf/chain/CChain.cpp

## CChain_TickChain / kyoshin/cf/chain/CChain — case 5 lbz/lfs is a scheduler height vs mem-dep tradeoff (Wii/1.1 -O4, 40.0%)
- Symptom:   same 11-insn tail set as retail; decomp `lfs; li 1; lbz; li 60; stfs; addi` vs retail `lbz; li 1; lfs; li 60; addi; stfs`. Witness slot 358 `lbz` vs `lfs`. Size `0x12c8` exact. objdiff ~97.4% / hexdiff 40.0% (634 structural / 87 reg_swap)
- Cause:     list-scheduler PickCandidate prefers the SDA21 `lfs` chain (higher latency) unless the `lbz`→`addi`→store chain is taller. An escaped `scratchB.field_6 = next` before the timer stores adds a mem-dep `stb → stfs`, so `lbz` wins and the prefix matches — but the extra `stb` sits in the `lfs` delay slot (and shifts the rest of the function unless a later wrap buy pays the 4B). Sinking that store makes `stfs → stb` and `lfs` wins again. `field_2 = next` first aliases `self`, so `stb field_2` precedes `lfs`. `paused = next - state` emits extra `rlwinm`+`subf`. Address-taken `field_2` and `paused`/`hold` locals do not flip the first pick
- Fix:       none this session — keep mixed wrap (`case 0xc` `idx += 1` / `(u8)(idx-1)`; `case 0xd` `idx +=`/`-=`) + `case 0x1a: return` + simple `next = state+1` then timer then `field_2 = next`
- Result:    40.0% / 0x12c8 / witness still `lbz` vs `lfs`. Next: register-only `addi` successor (no mem-dep into `stfs`), or a live-in/color change that makes the first pick `lbz`
- Evidence:  us-80279fbc / src/kyoshin/cf/chain/CChain.cpp

## CChain_TickChain / kyoshin/cf/chain/CChain — s8 second vreg flips PickCandidate to lbz; leftover extsb (Wii/1.1 -O4)
- Symptom:   `u8 raw; s8 state = (s8)raw; next = state+1` emits retail prefix `lbz; li 1; lfs; li 60` then `extsb` where retail has `addi r0,r3,1`. Witness would die at addi vs extsb, not lbz vs lfs
- Cause:     extra `extsb` raises the `lbz` chain height so PickCandidate prefers it over SDA21 `lfs`. The extra node occupies the `lfs` delay slot (`+0x05a8`). `int state = raw` coalesces (back to `lfs` first). ## CGXCache .sdata2 anon cast-pool tail — BiasDouble helpers retire drop_data_tail (Wii/1.1 -O4,p, 2026-09-19)
- Symptom:   raw `.sdata2` 0x11C8 vs retail 0x11B6 (+0x12 = anon `@N` s32/u32 int→f32 magics). Prefix `[:0x11B6]` already byte-identical; mid-pool already holds `lbl_eu_8066A388/A390` at +0x10/+0x18.

Hand-rolled `BiasDouble`/`s32ToF` (subtract named mid-pool doubles) uses `fsub`+`frsp` instead of retail builtin `fsubs`, so FULL on `bindTextureGX`/`updateOrthoGX` is lost (29%/35%). Defining the magics as TU-local `.sdata2` `f64` and using plain casts restores FULL insn but does **not** CSE `@N` onto the defined symbols (reloc stays `@N`, size +0x12).
- Fix:       route every live int→f32 site through BiasDouble helpers; retire `drop_data_tail` + `retarget_relocs` (freeze ratchet). Demote the two former FULLs to HIGH_MATCH.
- Result:    raw `.sdata2` MATCH 0x11B6; UnitRules shrink; bindTextureGX/updateOrthoGX HIGH_MATCH; split OVER +0x11C from helper codegen.
- Residual (Category C): simultaneous `fsubs` FULL + no `@N` tail is unreachable under UnitRules freeze (cannot re-add drop/retarget). EQUIVALENT fails (`fsub`≠`fsubs`). Keep helpers for the data gate.
- Confidence: repo_proven
- Applies to/a.k.a.: Category C drop burn-down; ADXT BiasDouble CSE does **not** transfer when the magic also lives as opaque mid-pool bytes / when `@N` is a separate cast-pool symbol.

## WUD .data auto jumptable @5780 — Category C keep drop (Wii/1.1 -O4,p, 2026-09-19)
- Symptom:   raw `.data` 0x11CC vs retail 0x11A8 (+0x24 = MWCC auto `@5780` switch table). Named `jumptable_80562FA0` mid-section (inject/retarget/zero). `__wudSecurityEventStackCallback` 96.2% (10 struct + 3 reg_swap), size 0x554/0x554 PASS.

- Result:    postprocess MATCH; Security near-miss recorded; raw data drop stays. Last structural angle (mid fp-table) falsified — retail dispatch is switch-into-self via mid-section JT, not an outlined handler table.
- Confidence: repo_proven
- Applies to/a.k.a.: mid-section retail jumptable vs MWCC auto-last invariant; fp-table outline destroys in-function `bctr` shape.

## CMenuSelectShop ctor — QuestLog null-ptmf walk with two occ sub-tables (Wii/1.1, pragma optimize_for_size, FULL_MATCH)
- Symptom:   26.7%, 29 structural + 15 reg_swap; decomp stored occ6c/occ70 early via direct `__ptmf_null[i]` indexing (two lis bases, plain lwz), retail keeps occ addr computations live in regs (addi pair) with stores late + single `lwzu r3,0(r10)` ptmf base.

Second-slot-first store order is scheduler-natural, not hand-ordered.
- Result:    FULL_MATCH 100.0%, 0 structural, 0 reg_swap, size 0xF0/0xF0 exact; TU 15/15, split PASS (0x0 spare), promoted to Matching.

## nw4r lyt split overage — what is source-fixable and what is linker dead-strip (GC/3.0a5.2, 2026-11-17)
- Symptom:   every lyt unit with all functions matching still fails the split-size gate (0xB8..0x35C over); 188 units repo-wide, 60,420 bytes.
- Cause:     three different things. (1) Real source errors: `Window` declared overrides of `FindAnimationLinkSelf(AnimTransform*)`, `SetAnimationEnable(AnimTransform*,bool,bool)` and `GetMaterial()` that the retail Window vtable does not have (retail slots point at the `Pane` versions; `Window::GetMaterial()` was declared but never defined = link undef). (2) Real out-of-line source functions that retail inlined into their only callers and mwld then dead-stripped (`Picture::Init/ReserveTexCoord/SetTexCoordNum/Picture(u8)`, `Window::InitContent/InitFrame/ReserveTexCoord`, `Pane::Init/InsertChild/GetPaneRect/SetUserData/CalculateMtxChild`, `PaneBase` ctor/dtor + `__vt__PaneBase`, `TexMap::SetNoWrap` x2); same-era reference source has them as ordinary non-inline definitions. (3) Compiler-generated, unreferenced weak/local destructors from the shared ut headers (`__dt__Q34nw4r2ut12LinkListNodeFv`, `__dt__...LinkList<T,N>Fv`, anon-namespace `NonCopyable` dtor, `__dt__Window::Content`): no relocation in the object references them and no retail copy exists anywhere in symbols.txt. The older `drop_text_symbols` UNIT_RULES for the hbm twins document the same orphans.
- Fix:       (1) removed the three bogus Window overrides (vtable relocs now equal retail; `GetContentMaterial` calls `static_cast<const Pane*>(this)->GetMaterial()`). (2)+(3) gate decision 2026-11-17 (PLAN §17.8): `weak_dedup.linked_view` now dead-strips functions with no retail copy that nothing retained references (unit must spell every retail `.text` symbol; force-active symbols are roots; local data stays; a nameless global vtable goes only when all its references are excluded and the unit's data slice is fully named). The `inline` markers tried first were reverted — source keeps the original out-of-line shape. Result: `run.py size --all` 188 -> 136 FAIL with no unit newly failing, `data diff --all` 447 -> 445; lyt_pane/lyt_animation/lyt_picture/lyt_window split 0x0 spare. `lbl_eu_80569C78` renamed `__vt__Q34nw4r3lyt18AnimTransformBasic` (US/EU) and the lyt_animation drop/rename UNIT_RULES fields retired. Pitfall: the cached linked object was keyed on the object bytes only, so a rule change reused stale views — key now includes the exclusion set.
- Also:      US splits.txt now gives lyt_group/lyt_layout/lyt_picture/lyt_textBox their own `.data` (vtable) and lyt_picture/lyt_textBox their own `.sbss` (typeInfo) instead of lyt_pane owning 0x805698F0-0x80569AB8; the hand-written fake vtable arrays and `lyt_pane_sbss_pad`/`lyt_picture_pad2` are deleted; stale `#Q34nw4r3lyt` UNIT_RULES fields that renamed real symbols back to raw labels or stripped now-owned `.data` are retired (shrink-only, frozen check OK, 4 fields awaiting --ratchet).
- Result:    lyt_picture 13/13 + split PASS + data MATCH + extab MATCH (promotion-ready; not promoted because the link cannot run while two unrelated kyoshin TUs fail to compile). lyt_group and lyt_layout data MATCH. lyt_window overage 0x250 -> 0x118. No function regressions across the 16 lyt units or CLibLayout.
- Evidence:  libs/nw4r/src/lyt/lyt_window.cpp, lyt_picture.cpp, lyt_pane.cpp; libs/nw4r/include/nw4r/lyt/lyt_window.h; config/us/splits.txt; tools/postprocess_reloc_names.py

## Postprocess rule burn-down, pass 1 — what retires mechanically and what does not (2026-11-17)
- Symptom:   `tools/postprocess_reloc_names.py` carried 301 rules; most exist because the source or the split, not the compiler, differs from retail.
- Cause:     four recurring stand-ins. (1) symbols.txt placeholder names (`lbl_eu_*`, `__ct__CCur18`, `...__Q23LOD9LODMemManFv`) where the compiled object already emits the real mangled name at the same address. (2) `.sdata2` splits that do not give a TU its own literal pool, so `pool_patterns`/`extern_data_sections` rename or strip it. (3) `extern const float lbl_eu_*;` declarations used in place of literals (2,921 declarations in 385 files), which leave the object with a partial pool. (4) functions the linker strips anyway (`drop_text_symbols`), now modelled by the linked view (PLAN §17.8).
- Fix:       (1) rename in symbols.txt, then `run.py targets sync-symbols`; convert the `extern "C"` definition to the real member. (2) give the TU its exact slice when the object's pool is a unique byte match AND a rule label or a fully-literal pool proves the address; unaligned slice ends are fine, do not "round" an already-exact slice. (3) replace the label with the retail value only once the TU owns its pool — a literal in a TU without its own slice scores as a reloc-name drift. (4) delete the field; size/data/extab gates stay unchanged.
- Result:    301 -> 280 rules; all 21 `drop_text_symbols` fields, 60 placeholder renames, 18 `.sdata2` pool fields retired. Link gate missing 96 -> 72. 13,107 -> 13,128 functions at 100%.
- MWCC:      a float tested for truth is `if (x)`, not `if (x != 0.0f)`: with a literal the explicit compare loads the constant first (`lfs f1,const; lfs f0,x`), the implicit test loads the member first as retail does (CScnBlend `Blend_DrawFilter`). Pass-through float wrappers (`CTaskLOD::notifyLODTick(float)`) need no "uninitialized float" trick once the signature carries the argument.
- Trap:      the link gate's `sda_reloc` count is not stable: mwld stops after ~100 errors ("too many link errors"), so retiring undefined symbols lets previously hidden small-data errors print (8 -> 14: g3d_resmat `GetLyrRate`, CfObjectEne `CActorParam_addHp`, both reference literals inside a range their rule drops).
- Open:      pseudo-constructors that call a member ctor through a fake C name (`__ct__CCur18(&self->mCur, 0)`) cannot be fixed with placement new (adds a null check); the owner needs a real constructor. `mCur = CCur18(arc);` replaces the temp + fake ctor/dtor block and usually matches. CMenuSelectShop demoted for this reason.
- Fix (2026-11-17): both units were fixed in source instead of raising the `sda_reloc` baseline. g3d_resmat: label externs and the hand-written trailing `.sdata2` block replaced by literals, rule deleted; the natural pool is `0.6, 0.0f, ...` where retail has `0.0f, 1.0f, 0.6, ...`, i.e. an earlier function using 0.0f/1.0f is missing from the source, so the unit is NonMatching until that is found. CfObjectEne: hand-built 0x70 pool (structs, `ene_f3..f10`, filler string, `CfEneF64Conv` conversions) replaced by literals and plain casts, rule deleted.
- Cause:     CfObjectEne's "0x70 pool" was two things. (1) The last 0x10 bytes (`lbl_eu_806669C8` 180.0f, `lbl_eu_806669D0` int->double magic) are referenced only by code_800B06A4/CfGameManager text: the `.sdata2` boundary was wrong; now 0x806669C8. (2) The `"ene1Lv"` string between 1.8f and 10.0f is the initializer of a file-scope `char*` (`lbl_eu_80661CB8`, in `.sdata`): MWCC puts a pointer-initializer string literal of <= 8 bytes in `.sdata2` at its source position among the float literals (longer ones go to `.rodata`, e.g. the sibling pointer `lbl_eu_80661CBC` -> `lbl_eu_804FC148`). Probe: `char* p = "ene1Lv";` after initEnemyBattleState reproduces the retail 0x60 pool byte-for-byte.
- Open:      CfObjectEne cannot define those two pointers yet: `.sdata` 0x80661CA0-0x80661CC8 (the pointers plus this TU's RTTI records) is split to code_800B06A4.cpp and the unit emits no classes. Its pool is therefore 8 bytes short and `lbl_eu_80666974` is a recorded link-gate missing symbol (added by hand to the baseline; 10 others retired in the same ratchet). initEnemyBattleState dropped 93.3 -> 82.9 in the report: with real literals MWCC keeps `self + 0x3E9C` in a callee-saved register across the four calls; the earlier score depended on loading the two floats from the fake pool struct. Retail recomputes the adjustment per call (implicit base-class `this` adjustment); `static_cast` through the `...At3E9C` MI views adds null checks and is worse. Needs the real class hierarchy.
- Evidence:  config/us/symbols.txt, config/us/splits.txt, tools/postprocess_reloc_names.py, src/kyoshin/CCur.cpp, libs/monolib/src/lod/{CTaskLOD,LODMemMan}.cpp, libs/monolib/src/scn/CScnBlend.cpp, libs/nw4r/src/g3d/res/g3d_resanmchr.cpp

## Source-faithfulness pass — split ownership from relocations, and the first de-faked unit (2026-11-17)
- Symptom:   units byte-match while the source is not what was written: storage and constants defined in a neighbour TU as `lbl_eu_*` fillers, hand-built vtables/RTTI, hand-written static initialisers, rules that rename or drop what the compiler emitted.
- Tooling:   `run.py faithful` scores every unit (labels, `extern "C"` mangled names, `__declspec(section)`, raw offset casts, view structs, postprocess rule, foreign data) against `docs/evidence/faithful_baseline.json`, shrink-only. `tools/coop/section_owners.py` infers data ownership from the retail split objects' relocations (a data symbol referenced by exactly one unit's `.text` votes for that unit; votes kept by longest run consistent with text link order).
- Rule:      only anonymous symbols are evidence. Tier A = anonymous `.sdata2`/`.sbss2` literals, jump tables, anonymous strings (78 split range edits applied). Named symbols never move a boundary: `ml::huge`, `__EXIFreq`, `bta_dm_pm_cfg`, `bd_addr_null` are globals defined in one TU and used only by another, and moving them was wrong (reverted).
- Signal:    a `.sdata2` unit start that is not 8-aligned, or an anonymous literal referenced by two units, means either a named constant (`nw4r::snd::detail::EnvGenerator::VOLUME_INIT`, now a real `const volatile f32`) or one TU split into several units (22 groups, e.g. CfCollCircle/AABB/Cylinder/CapsuleImpl + CfObjectColl) - a text split error, not a data one.
- MWCC:      `char* p = "ene1Lv";` puts a string of 8 bytes or fewer in `.sdata2` at source position; local `GXColor c = {...}` initialisers also live in `.sdata2`. A literal passed directly to a call is reloaded each time, while a `float x = 0.0f` local used across a loop is hoisted into a saved FPR. `(f32)(s32)mtRand()` reproduces the signed int->float magic. An inline helper's int argument must be a named local at the call site (`int volDb = (int)(100.0f * vol); lookupVolume(volDb);`): passing the cast expression re-materialises the `fctiwz` store/load at every use inside the inlined loop.
- Fix (CLibCriStreamingPlay): the regressions after replacing label externs with literals were source errors the labels had hidden. The volume table lookup compared the wrong way (`volDb < hi` for retail's `volDb >= hi`); wkUpdate used double arithmetic where retail is single; three hand-expanded pause computations are one inlined helper (`applyPause`); the fade timer is `entry->field_0x74 += 1/30` re-read from the struct, and the fade action is signed. Two symbols were misnamed: retail `func_8045C700` (0x80460744) is `setStreamVolume` and retail `setStreamVolume` (0x804608F4) is `setStreamVolumeScale`, as `CLibCri`'s forwarders already said; renamed in US/EU symbols, callers and targets. wkUpdate 80.4 -> 88.2, setStreamPause 99.1, setStreamVolume 99.7, setStreamVolumeScale 99.3.
- Fix (CERand): the unit hand-built its vtables/RTTI under `lbl_eu_*` names, kept a never-called `KeepCERandomizerEmission()` to force the inline virtuals out, hand-wrote `__sinit`, and had its two global objects defined as byte arrays in CNReqtaskSave.cpp (`u8 lbl_eu_80660028[16]`) and CNReqtaskCheck.cpp (`u32 lbl_eu_80665A08[2]`). Replaced by `CERandomizer ceRandomizer; CERandomizerSimple ceRandomizerSimple;` at the top of the TU and calls through them (`ceRandomizer.randFHalf()`); MWCC devirtualises and inlines exactly as retail, emits the vtables/RTTI/sinit itself in retail order, and places the weak inline virtuals where retail has them. `.bss` 0x80660028-0x80660038 and `.sbss` 0x80665A08-0x80665A10 moved to CERand in splits; seven symbols renamed (`ceRandomizer`, `ceRandomizerSimple`, `__vt__*`, `__RTTI__*`); rule deleted. 16/16 functions, size PASS, data/extab MATCH, faithful score 0. `drawMarkerEntry`'s "default clamp-info blob" `lbl_eu_80665A08` was `&ceRandomizer`.
- Recipe:    for a unit with hand-built vtable/RTTI data: (1) find its real globals by looking at what `__sinit_\<unit>_cpp` stores in the retail asm; (2) give the unit the `.bss`/`.sbss` ranges of those globals and delete the filler definitions from whichever unit carried them; (3) rename the vtable/RTTI/global symbols in symbols.txt to what MWCC emits; (4) declare the globals in source order of the sinit stores and call members through them; (5) delete the rule. If the compiler's own emission order differs from retail, the class or global declaration order is wrong - do not reorder data by hand.
- Open:      `Chain_CheckChanceRoll` 63.9 -> 60.7 after replacing a union int->float hack with real casts (accepted). CNReqtaskSave extab gate failure (`CNReqSaveConfigSave`/`sinit_804DAF58` naming, hand-built vtables) predates this pass. wkUpdate still re-reads `entry->flags` where retail does (0x10 short).
- Evidence:  tools/coop/{faithful,section_owners}.py, config/us/{splits,symbols}.txt, libs/monolib/src/effect/CERand.cpp, libs/monolib/src/lib/CLibCriStreamingPlay.cpp, libs/monolib/src/lib/CLibCriMoviePlay.cpp, libs/nw4r/src/snd/snd_EnvGenerator.cpp

## RTTI names recovered from retail data; why "-RTTI off" and `drop_data_tail` exist (2026-11-17)
- Symptom:   de-faking a unit (real classes instead of hand-built vtable arrays) leaves its data larger than retail: extra `__RTTI__<Base>` records, base lists and name strings for every base class. 21 units are compiled with `-RTTI off` and ~13 rules carry `drop_data_tail`/`drop_data_range` to hide this.
- Cause:     not a source problem. MWCC emits a weak type_info for every polymorphic class a TU touches and mwld keeps the first copy; the retail split objects come from the linked DOL and so show one copy only. `tools/coop/lib/weak_dedup.py` already models this, but it identifies the surviving retail copy by name, and only 61 retail type_info records had names - the rest were `lbl_eu_*`.
- Fix:       `tools/coop/rtti_names.py` rebuilds `__RTTI__<mangled>` from the retail objects: an anonymous 8-byte `.sdata`/`.data` symbol whose first word points at a labelled NUL-terminated string (same object or, across a split boundary, another one), whose second word is a relocation or null, and which a vtable or base list in `.data` points at. 484 records are now named in config/us/symbols.txt (was 61). 236 were renamed directly; 187 more were renamed together with their spelling in hand-built source data (`__RTTI__...` is a valid C identifier).
- Trap:      a hand-declared `extern ... __RTTI__8CProcess;` in a TU where the compiler also generates that type_info is error 10322 "illegal name overloading" - the same error the `-RTTI off` comments in configure.py cite. 56 labels were left as `lbl_eu_*` for that reason (everything declared in a shared header, plus CDeviceGX, CCur, CTaskLOD, CfObjectEff, CDeviceFontInfoExt, CNBanner and the four named in rule values). They get their names when the unit's hand-built typeinfo is deleted. Template classes (142, e.g. `CTTask<CTaskGame>`, `reslist<CScn *>`) are not recovered: the string is the demangled spelling.
- Result:    no function changed score; 25 data sections improved. CTaskManager: hand-built vtables/RTTI removed by a Haiku agent, 16/16 functions (was 14/16), rule deleted, `-RTTI off` removed; its `.data` is retail's plus weak copies of `__RTTI__8CProcess`/`14CChildListNode`/`15CDoubleListNode`, which stay visible until those three retail records are named (blocked on CTaskLOD.cpp's hand declarations).
- Agents:    first batch of six narrow Haiku agents, one hand-faked unit each (recipe in the previous entry). Done: lyt_resourceAccessor (real class, compiler vtable, rule deleted), snd_Lfo (sine table is a function-local `static const s8 sinTable[33]`, rule deleted), CTaskManager. Stopped with a root cause rather than a hack: CProc (`-RTTI off`), HBMAnmController and CLibStaticData (weak base RTTI = the dedup case above; CLibStaticData's singletons are fillers in CLibLayout.cpp:344).
- Also:      bta_dm_act.c declared `btm_cb` as a 2-byte struct, so MWCC addressed the 0x27C4-byte `.bss` object through r13 (a hidden small-data link error that surfaced when another undefined symbol retired); it now has its retail size.
- Next:      (1) name the template type_infos and `__vt__` symbols the same way; (2) delete hand-built typeinfo unit by unit, dropping `-RTTI off` (`run.py faithful` counts `rtti_off`); (3) rules of the form `("__RTTI__9CDeviceGX", "lbl_eu_80663758")` rename the compiler's correct name to a label and die with the label.
- Evidence:  tools/coop/rtti_names.py, tools/coop/faithful.py, config/us/symbols.txt, configure.py (CTaskManager), libs/monolib/src/core/CTaskManager.cpp, libs/nw4r/src/snd/snd_Lfo.cpp, libs/nw4r/src/lyt/lyt_resourceAccessor.cpp

## NAND family rebuilt from three merged TUs; the "sinit + vtable-storing func" pattern is a static task object (2026-11-17)
- Symptom:   `CNReqtaskSave.cpp` held ~40 functions under invented names (`CNReqSaveConfigSave`, `sinit_804DAF58` + `func_804DAF60`), hand-built vtables, `noinline`/`optimize_for_size` pragmas, a postprocess rule, and an extab gate failure. `monolib_eu_804F9E98.cpp` and parts of CNBanner.cpp/CNand.cpp were the same family under other names.
- Cause:     the unit was three retail TUs: `CNReqtask.cpp` (async NAND wrappers and shared state), `CNRequest.cpp` (one queued request: picks a task and steps it), `CNReqtaskSave.cpp`. Each `CNReqtask<X>` (Check, Save, Load, Remove, Readdir, Createdir, SaveBanner) is its own TU. RTTI name strings gave the class names; 8-byte padding between objects and the order of name strings in `.rodata` gave the TU boundaries. `monolib_eu_804F9E98` is `CNReqtaskCreatedir` (its RTTI string says so).
- MWCC:      `static CNReqtaskX sTask;` for a class with an implicit constructor emits `__sinit_\File_cpp` (`addi r3, sTask; b __ct__`) followed by a weak out-of-line `__ct__NNClassFv` that stores the vtable. That is the retail shape ~150 units reproduce by hand as `sinit_XXXX` + `func_XXXX` ("Dissolved monolibdata2 / blob surgery"). Write the class and the static object; delete the hand-built vtable, RTTI and sinit.
- MWCC:      `#pragma no_static_dtors on` around a global object gives a constructor call in `__sinit` with no `__register_global_object` (CNand `nand`). Function-local statics are `@LOCAL@func@name` / `@GUARD@func@name`. The vptr sits where the first virtual is declared. RTTI name strings are emitted at the key function; function-body literals pool at the end of `.rodata`.
- MWCC:      a `setup(void* p, ...)` that casts to a local `Param*` keeps the parameter block in r31 as retail does; taking `Param*` directly swaps the callee-saved registers. `mHead++; mHead %= 8;` (s16) gives extsh before the modulo; `(mHead + 1) % 8` does not.
- MWCC:      every "needs `noinline`" note in the old unit was an artefact of the merge: across real TU boundaries nothing can be inlined. With the unit's real flags (`-O4,s`) the size pragmas were unnecessary too.
- MWCC:      MSL declares C library functions as unable to throw (`_MSL_CANT_THROW`). Without it a `memset` in a constructor opens an exception range with a DESTROYBASE action that retail does not have (CNBanner ctor: record `10080000 00000000`). `string.h` now carries the attribute.
- MWCC:      `CNBanner::~CNBanner() { unload(); }` with `unload` defined later in the file inlines to the retail destructor (base+offset `lbzu` walk included) and gives retail's single exception range. The earlier hand-expanded body matched the code but produced two ranges and four chained actions: a matching function with a wrong extab record usually means the source has the wrong shape.
- Tooling:   `weak_dedup._dead_strip` drops a `__vt__` object that has no retail name and that no relocation in its own object references (abstract base `CNReqtask`: emitted at its key function `close`, never installed out of line, absent from retail). Other unreferenced nameless data is still left alone. Tests in `tools/coop/tests/test_weak_dedup.py`.
- Result:    CNand 14/14, CNReqtask 20/20, CNRequest 9/9, seven task units and CNBanner 9/9: sizes PASS, data MATCH, extab MATCH; three rules deleted; fillers for this family removed from CWorkSystemCache, CETrail, CMdlDynamics, main.cpp.
- Fix:       `CNReqtask::error` reported through an `extern "C"` `logExceptionMessage__10CExceptionFv`; it is now the static member `CException::logExceptionMessage(const wchar_t*)` (`...FPCw`), still 100%. Retail tests only the first byte of the wide string.
- Open:      EU/JP splits still describe the merged unit (only US is built). CNBanner still needs `IWORK_EVENT_INLINE_DTOR`, a macro that gives IWorkEvent two definitions.
- Evidence:  libs/monolib/{include/monolib,src}/nand/, config/us/{splits,symbols}.txt, tools/coop/lib/weak_dedup.py, libs/PowerPC_EABI_Support/include/stl/string.h

## CTTask users: the hand-built constructor is a real constructor plus `create` (2026-11-17)
- Symptom:   link gate, two new undefined `@N` locals referenced from CfTaskMain after `__RTTI__8CProcess` / `__RTTI__14CChildListNode` / `__RTTI__15CDoubleListNode` got their names (retail copies at 0x80661948/50/58, in CTaskGameCf's slice): the unit's rule stripped `.data/.rodata/.sdata` while its weak type_infos still pointed at the stripped name strings.
- Cause:     CfTaskMain was a fake: `__ct__800697E8` called the raw CProcess constructor, wrote both vtable pointers through a byte-range shim and copied `__ptmf_null` word by word through a volatile pointer.
- Fix:       `CfTaskMain(CScn* scene) : mScene(scene) {}` and `static CfTaskMain* create(CProcess* parent, CScn* scene) { CfTaskMain* task = new (CWorkThreadSystem::getWorkMem()) CfTaskMain(scene); task->Regist(parent, false); return task; }`. 11/11, extab MATCH, rule deleted, unit promoted to Matching. The three CfGameManager functions it calls take no object in retail and are now `static` members.
- Fix (CTaskLOD): hand-built vtables, base lists, RTTI records and name strings deleted; the compiler's own are byte-identical (data MATCH). `create` was 93.8%: retail runs the persistent-buffer setup inside the null check of `new`, so that code belongs to the constructor, not to `create`. 38/38.
- MWCC:      retail order for every CTTask user is `CTTask<X>::~CTTask`, the class's own functions, `create`, then `CTTask<X>::Move` / `Draw`. With the destructor specialization at the end of the file the code matches and the exception index does not.
- Trap:      a TU that hand-declares `extern "C" u32 __RTTI__8CProcess[]` and also sees the real class with RTTI on fails with 10322. Of 16 files using the three labels only CTaskLOD did; the answer was to delete its hand-built tables.
- Next:      64 files use CTTask and 32 carry explicit specializations and usually a shim constructor like the one removed here. Same recipe; `CTTask.hpp` still declares Move/Draw/dtor without bodies so that the specializations are emitted.
- Evidence:  src/kyoshin/cf/CfTaskMain.{cpp,hpp}, libs/monolib/src/lod/CTaskLOD.cpp, libs/monolib/src/core/CException.cpp, config/us/symbols.txt, docs/evidence/{link_undefs,extab,text_order,faithful}_baseline.json

## CTTask batch 2: private interface bases, `IUICf`, and a class cut in half by its split (2026-11-17)
- Scope:     six Haiku agents, one hand-built CTTask constructor each (CTaskGameEffAfter, CTaskGameEvt, CMenuItem, CCol6Invite, CMenuGCItem, CMenuTitle). Two finished with help, one exposed a split error, three stopped and restored.
- MWCC:      the RTTI base list names only **public** bases. CTaskGameEvt's retail list is `CDoubleListNode, CChildListNode, CProcess, CTTask<CTaskGameEvt>` with no IWorkEvent/IScnRender although both thunk sets exist, so the class is `class CTaskGameEvt : public CTTask<CTaskGameEvt>, IWorkEvent, IScnRender` (interfaces private by default). A base list that is too long by 8 bytes per interface means a missing access specifier, not a missing base. CMenuItem's list does include IScnRender, so there it is public.
- MWCC:      per-function `#pragma optimize_for_size` plus `__declspec(noinline)` on the constructor was standing in for the unit flag `-O4,s`: with it the out-of-line constructor, `stmw`/`lmw` frames and `create` all match with no pragma (CTaskGameEvt 18/18, data MATCH, extab MATCH).

Retail CInfoCf ends at 0x801679F4 (8 functions, 2 extab records); everything after is CMenuItem.cpp. Splits (US, EU text/extab) and sources now follow that; one `class CMenuItem : public IUICf, public IScnRender` with a real inline constructor, `static create`, `static sInstance`, compiler thunks and string literals.
- Open (CMenuItem): 9/18 in the report. `create` is byte-identical but names `__vt__14CTTask<5IUICf>` where symbols.txt still says `lbl_eu_8052BF70`; the label cannot be renamed until the hand-built users (CMainMenu, CMiniMap, COption, CMenuMakeCrystal, CMenuShopBuy, CMenuSkipTimer) stop spelling it. `~CMenuItem` is 75%: retail's has no vtable stores and two redundant null checks, i.e. an empty body with a real `CItemBoxGrid` member and inline `~IUICf` / `~CTTask<IUICf>`. `Init` and the six `InfoCfCopy*` functions are `member = Temp(...)` assignments and the implicit `operator=` of CItemBoxGrid's members. All of that waits on CItemBoxGrid (6,000 lines of C-style code with a postprocess rule) becoming a class: leaf first.

CMenuTitle has a second `class CMenuTitle` in `CUIErrMesWin.hpp` whose methods sit in CUIErrMesWin's split (another split error).

## Vtable/RTTI ownership, thunks as TU terminators, and real locals for exception tables (2026-11-18)

**Vtable runs sat in the wrong unit's `.data`.** A scan of every retail unit object for
vtables whose destructor slot is *undefined in that object* found 69 misassigned vtables;
in almost every case a unit's `.data`/`.sdata` began with the vtable + RTTI of the class
defined by the text-previous unit. 56 boundaries were moved (only adjacent, contiguous
cases). MWCC emits `[vtable][RTTI base list]` in that order, so a small `n*8+4`-byte
object that references only RTTI symbols and sits *before* a vtable is the base list of
the *previous* class (e.g. the 0xC list before `__vt__Q22cf8CREvtObj` belongs to
`cf::CREvtEffect`), not part of the following vtable. Two nw4r/g3d proposals were wrong
(the matching nw4r sources emit that data where it was) and were not applied.

**What the move exposed.** Units marked `Matching` that "owned" no vtable because the
neighbour's split supplied it: `cf::CREvtObj` and `cf::CREvtMem` were converted to real
classes (ctor with init list, `virtual ~T()`, class `operator new/delete` for CREvtObj)
and still match 100%, now with matching data. `CLoad.cpp` and `CMenuOption.cpp` contained
hand-written copies of *another class's* vtable (`CTutorialList`, `CTutorial`) — deleted.
`CfObjectEne`, `CfObjectImplNpc` and `CfResTboxImpl` use the manual-vtable scheme for
classes they own and were demoted to `NonMatching` until the classes are real.
`CfObjectImplObj.cpp` emitted C++-mangled names for functions whose retail symbols are
unmangled; it only linked because nothing referenced them from a compiled object.

**This-adjusting thunks end a translation unit.** MWCC emits `@N@...` thunks after
everything else in the TU. Functions that follow a unit's thunks in retail text belong to
the next TU: four `cf::UnkClass_80192BF4` functions after `CMenuPTState`'s thunks became
their own unit (`kyoshin/cf/code_80194310`), and the 0x40 destructor after
`CMenuQuestLog`'s thunks is the destructor of `CMenuSymbolMark`'s +0x70 member (named as
such by a DESTROYMEMBER action in the SymbolMark constructor's exception table).

**Exception-table records identify real locals.** A retail record with a destroy-local
action whose destructor is a "free function" means the original had a real object:
- `nw4r::lyt::DrawInfo drawInfo;` instead of `u8 buf[0x54]` + C-style ctor/dtor calls
  keeps `cbRenderBefore` at 100% and fixes its record (CMenuTitle, CMenuItem; the
  remaining ~35 units are being converted).
- The "enum list holder" (`CTaskGame_enumListCtor` / `__dt__80043E88`) is a real class,
  `CfEnumListHolder`. A scan loop that exits early with the holder alive matched only as
  an inline helper returning `bool` (early `return` inside the loop), not as a
  `goto`/flag in the caller.

**Member dtor shape.** A menu destructor that is 0x14 bytes too long and stores its own
vtable pointers has an explicit member-destructor call in its body; the retail shape is a
real member with a declared out-of-line destructor and an empty `~Menu() {}`
(CMenuMakeCrystal, CMenuPlayAward, CMenuEnemyState, CMenuPTState, CMenuMapSelect,
CMenuArtsSet).

**Open: implicit `operator=` inlining.** `mX = X(args)` rebuilds match when the member
class's implicit assignment has one use site in the TU; with several use sites MWCC emits
an out-of-line weak `__as__` and calls it, while retail has the copies inlined
(CMenuPlayAward `CCur18`/`CScrollBar`/entry array, CMenuMapSelect). Unverified
hypothesis: those classes declare an explicit inline `operator=`.

## Widget re-init is assignment from a temporary (2026-11-18)

The menu `Init` functions that build a stack widget, copy it field by field into
a member and destroy the stack copy are plain assignments in the original
source:

```cpp
mBgTex = CBgTex(0);
mTitleAHelp = CTitleAHelp(name, 0x50);
```

MWCC inlines the implicit `operator=` of the outer class (scalar members become
load/store pairs in declaration order, the vptr is skipped) and calls the
member's user-declared `operator=` out of line — that is the
`bl __as__17UnkClass_8045F564FRC17UnkClass_8045F564` in every such block. The
temporary's constructor and `__dt__(…, -1)` calls come from the temporary
itself. Verified on `CMenuCollepedia::Init`: the two-line form compiles to the
same bytes as the ~25 hand-written lines it replaced.

Consequences:

- A hand-written `u8 temp[N]; __ct__…(temp); …copies…; __dt__…(temp, -1);`
  block is a sign that the destination should be a real, typed member.
- Small helpers named like `…CopyCursor(dst, src)` that such blocks call are
  the weak out-of-line `operator=` of a member class (for example a `CBaseCur`
  subclass), not hand-written utilities.
- Earlier note about implicit `operator=` being emitted out of line when used
  at more than one site still needs a unit where that happens to be checked
  against this form.

Follow-up from converting more units (same day):

- The assignment form only reproduces retail stack offsets when *every*
  temp-copy block in the function is a real temporary. Mixing one real
  temporary with a remaining raw `u8 temp[N]` buffer reorders the stack slots
  (`CMenuMapSelectSC::Init`: temp at `sp+8` instead of retail `sp+48`;
  `CMenuTutorial::Init` dropped from 100% to 12%). Convert a function's blocks
  together, after the member classes involved are real.
- Open: `CMenuItemExchange::Init` matches with the copies *out of line*
  (`ItemEx_CopyBgTex`, `ItemEx_CopyTitle`, `ItemEx_CopyLine`, `ItemEx_CopyGrid`
  sit right after `Init` in first-use order, i.e. they look like the weak
  implicit `operator=` bodies). Writing `mBgTex = CBgTex(0);` there inlines the
  copy and grows `Init` from 0x1BC to 0x244. Units where the copy is inlined
  (`CMenuCollepedia`, `CMenuKizunaTalkList`, `CMenuItem`) use the same flags.
  Untested hypothesis: with all four assignments real, the two very large ones
  (`CItemBoxLine` 0x388 bytes, `CItemBoxGrid` 0x638 bytes of copy code) push
  the caller past the inliner's size limit and none is inlined. Needs
  `CItemBoxLine`/`CItemBoxGrid` as real classes to test.

## Implicit operator= of a polymorphic widget is out of line and nothrow (CScrollBar, 2026-11-18)

- Making `CScrollBar` a real `IWorkEvent` subclass made its implicit
  `operator=` non-trivial. MWCC emits it as a weak out-of-line
  `__as__10CScrollBarFRC10CScrollBar` (memberwise, vptr skipped, 0xB4 bytes)
  right after its first user — that is the retail "copyScrollBarData" at
  0x8011D474 behind `CMenuQuestLog::Init`. Renamed, scope:weak.
- Calls to compiler-generated functions are known nothrow: `CMenuQuestLog::Init`
  written as `mQstLogList = CQstLogList((u16)field_2280);` has no extab actions
  (retail `0808000000000000`), as long as every nested copy is compiler
  generated too. One remaining `extern "C" __as__17UnkClass_8045F564…` call in
  the CSortMenu mirror's inline `operator=` added a destroy-temp action;
  replacing it with a real `UnkClass_8045F564` assignment removed it.
- Explicit padding members copied by the implicit `operator=` (CQstLogList
  `pad_0171`) break the match: delete them. An 8-byte record with a
  destructor (CQstLogList QstInfo, retail dtor `__dt__80227030`) is copied
  fieldwise (`lhz` + six `lbz`), i.e. memberwise, not as two words.
- Inlining is not uniform: the out-of-line call to `__as__10CScrollBar…` stays
  out of line in `CMenuQuestLog::Init` (nested in another implicit op=) and in
  `CTutorialList::CTutorialList` (-O4,s TU), but MWCC inlines it at the direct
  `mScrollBar = CScrollBar(1)` in `CQstLogList::CQstLogList` (default-flag TU
  with `#pragma optimize_for_size`) and in `ItemEx_CopyLine`, where retail
  calls it. Same for the QstInfo copy (`copyQstInfo` out of line in the
  retail CQstLogList ctor, inlined in retail Init). `#pragma auto_inline off`
  had no effect; `#pragma dont_inline on` outlines everything (too much).
  Open; suspect per-TU inliner flags.
- Explicit `p->~CScrollBar()` on a raw buffer becomes a virtual call once the
  class is polymorphic; use `p->CScrollBar::~CScrollBar()` or, better, a real
  temporary.

## Locals in destructors change the exception table, not the code (2026-11-18)

Found while making `cf::CREvtLight` and `cf::CREvtCamera` real subclasses of
`cf::CREvtObj`; in both cases the code was already 100% and only the extab
record differed.

- A function-scope copy of a member (`void* old = field_20;`) in a destructor
  produced five chained destroy-base actions. Using the member directly gives
  retail's single action.
- Block-scope `f32 x, y, z` inside a nested `if` in a destructor split the
  destroy-base range three ways. Declaring them once at the top of the
  destructor (`f32 z, y, x;`) gives retail's single range.
- `u32` parameters mangle as `Ul` with this compiler (`__ct__Q22cf10CREvtLightFUl`).
- The 0x10-byte object after a derived class's vtable that points at the
  base's `__RTTI__` is the derived class's base list and belongs to its unit
  (it had been split into the following unit, `CBgTex`, and reproduced there
  by a hand-written array).

## cf::CREvtModel family (CREvtModel / Map / Obj / Pc / CREvtEffect)

- Private bases are left out of the RTTI base list. CREvtModelMap/Pc/Obj base lists
  name only `cf::CREvtModel`, so `IWorkEvent` and `CScheduleChild` are private bases.
- In MWCC data order a class's `[vtable][base list]` means the base list starts the
  next unit's `.data` split. Example: the CScnMaruShadowNw4r base list (weak RTTI from
  the `dynamic_cast` in `setupShadow`) at 0x80531670 is the first CREvtModel object.
- When a virtual overrides only a secondary-base slot, the secondary vtable gets an
  `@<adj>@name` thunk and the whole vtable object also gets a direct slot appended at
  its end. Thunks are emitted at the end of the TU.
- A pointer-to-member constant `{0,-1,fn}` is emitted once per use, as an `@N` object
  in `.data` in first-use order. Retail names these `lbl_eu_*`, so functions that use
  them stay ✗ at 100% bytes because only the reloc name differs. Seen in Obj's ctor and
  vfunc_10, and in Pc's ctor, isBusy, loadFiles and checkLoaded.
- Compiler RTTI and string literals come after all user-defined data, so hand-placed
  data cannot be interleaved with them.
- `CScheduleChild` is `{ virtual ~CScheduleChild(){}; virtual void
  OnScheduleDelete(CSchedule*) = 0; }`. Its implicit inline dtor makes each user TU
  emit a weak `__dt__14CScheduleChildFv` and `__vt__14CScheduleChild`, and adds
  destroy-base extab actions. This is why CREvtEffect `.data` is 0x58 vs 0x48 and has
  one extra extab record. Retail's out-of-line copy is `__dt__80081C20` (the
  CfGameManagerUnityHelpers DEFINE_POD_DTOR). It has not been renamed yet.
- `mFlags` reload: retail reloads `this->mFlags` between `if (mFlags & X)` and the
  `mFlags |= / &= X` that follows. This happens in CREvtModel::vfunc_1C, Obj
  releaseAnims/stepProbe and Pc releaseAnims/initCounter. Plain source caches the
  value. `volatile u32 mFlags` reproduces the reload, and all five functions reach
  100%. The cost is the CREvtModel ctor: retail `mFlags(0)` + `mFlags |= 8` folds to
  `ori r0,r4,8`, which volatile cannot produce, so the ctor scores 69.7% (scheduling
  and register order only). The real access shape is still open; it may be an inline
  flag accessor. The old code used `*(volatile u32*)` casts for the same effect.

## Copy-function shape, nested implicit operator=, and overload pitfalls (QstInfo / TalkListEntry)

- A fieldwise copy taking a **non-const** reference (`QstInfo(QstInfo&)`) is emitted with load/store pairs interleaved, because the source may alias the destination. The same body with a `const&` source is scheduled, with all the loads hoisted. Retail CMenuQstCnt has both shapes as separate weak functions, so both ctors exist in the source.
- When an implicit class operator= copies an array member, it **calls** the element's out-of-line `operator=` only if that operator= has already been generated in the TU by a direct use somewhere. Placement in the file does not matter. Otherwise the element copy is inlined. An inline operator= declared in the header but never called does not trigger generation. Verified with CQstLogList ctor `mQstData = QstData();`.
- An element type that declares both `operator=(X&)` and `operator=(const X&)` makes MWCC reject the containing class's implicit array operator= with "illegal operands". TalkListEntry's non-const copy is therefore a named member (`Copy`), not an overload.
- Weak emission order is first-use order. With operator= left implicit, TalkListEntry emits fill ctor, `Copy`, then `__as__`, which matches retail.

## CItemBoxInfo / CItemBoxInfo2 / CNumSelect real classes; CItemBoxLine ctor temporaries (2026-11-18)

- **Copy-init versus assignment from a by-value return.** `T x = Func();` makes the call write
  straight into the local, then copies with the retail 8-byte-pair `mtctr` loop.
  `x = Func();` copies field by field instead. The Info2 RenderKind2/3 and Info1 RenderKind2/3
  record locals use copy-init (Info2 RenderKind2 went from 82% to 91.7%).
- **Struct copy scalarisation.** MWCC copies a struct with many scalar fields one field at a
  time. If the struct ends in a single array (CItemBoxCompRecord `u8 flags[4][7]`), it copies
  the scalar head and then runs a `mtctr` pair loop over the array.
- **Hand-written string pools stay undefined externs.** If the CItemBoxInfo pool
  (`lbl_eu_805063BC`) is defined in the TU, at either the top or the end, register allocation
  changes across many functions. Keep it extern and keep the blob inside the rodata struct.
  The cost is that the compiler RTTI name strings land after the pool, so `.rodata` cannot
  match until the pool becomes literals.
- **Store order in the ctor init list.** Retail CItemBoxInfo/2 ctors store all 20 slot panes,
  then mActive/mState/..., and call the page last. That needs 20 individually named
  `Pane*` members in the init list; a loop or array does not give the order. The page
  (CItemBoxPage) has no ctor. The Info ctors end with a call to the empty out-of-line
  `CItemBoxPage::Reset()` (0x801D5ACC). Both ctors match 100%.
- **Layout evidence from the implicit `operator=`.** CItemBoxLine's ctor does
  `mInfo2 = CItemBoxInfo2(kind, field394);`. In the copy, retail skips +0xAE, so CItemBoxInfo2
  has no `mFlagAE` (only CItemBoxInfo does). Retail also copies the page tail as one
  0x80-byte block from +0xD9 and copies nothing after +0x159. Both this ctor and
  `ShopBuy_CopyData` show it, so the real CItemBoxPage tail is `u8 sel; char name[0x80];`. The
  decomp still declares `mName[0x67]` + `s16 mValues2[12]`, because CItemBoxLine::RefreshPageList
  writes s16s at page+0x140 (open).
- **Return type of state getters.** Callers of `CItemBoxInfo{,2}::GetState` compare the result
  without `clrlwi`. Declare the return as `u32`, not `u8`. With `u8`, CItemBoxLine
  GetSelectReady/RefreshLineState and CItemBoxGrid IsItemBoxReady each gain a mask.
- **Member writes through a local page pointer.** CItemBoxLine::BuildPageData keeps retail
  register allocation only when the `mPage` stores go through a local
  `CItemBoxPage* page = &mPage;` (29.5%). Writing `mPage.x[i]` directly gives 4%.
- **Out-of-line weak `operator=` in CMenuItemExchange.** `ItemEx_CopyBgTex/CopyTitle/CopyLine/
  CopyGrid` sit directly after `Init` and are almost certainly the classes' weak operator=s.
  Our compile inlines the implicit `CItemBoxLine::operator=` (Init grows from 0x1BC to 0x5D8),
  so that unit keeps the explicit `ItemEx_CopyLine` call. CMenuShopBuy inlines the line copy in
  retail too, except for the page (ShopBuy_CopyData). There, `mItemBoxLine = CItemBoxLine(...)`
  matches the size (0x664). The ctor and dtor match once CItemBoxLine is a real member.

## When MWCC inlines a copy assignment (and any inline function): two rules (2026-11-18)

Question: why is the same class's `operator=` inlined in one TU and called out of
line (weak `__as__…`, emitted right after its first user) in another? Answer: two
independent inliner rules, both measured with stand-alone test TUs compiled with
the project flags (`-O4,p -inline auto -ipa file …` plus the unit's extra flags).
Neither depends on declaration order, on `#pragma auto_inline`, or on
`-inline level=N/deferred/smart` (all tried, no effect).

**Rule A: under `-O4,s`, an inline function with more than one call site in the
TU is not inlined anywhere.**

- `struct W { virtual ~W(); R r; int x, y; W(int); };` with `w = W(0);` in
  `M::Init` and `w = W(1);` in `M::Init2`: `-O4,s` emits weak `__as__1WFRC1W`
  after `Init` and both functions call it. `-O4,p` (or `-O4,s -O4,p`) inlines
  both. With one call site, `-O4,s` inlines it.
- Only trivial bodies escape it. `{R r; int x;}` (one call + one copy) is still
  inlined at two sites; `{R r; int x, y;}` and a POD `{int a, b;}` are not.
- It applies to explicit `inline` functions as well: `inline void f(int x)`
  with three stores and two callers becomes weak `f__Fi` at `-O4,s`.
- Call sites are counted over the whole TU (`-ipa file`). That includes:
  - sites inside other compiler-generated functions. `CScrollBar` assigned
    directly and again inside the implicit `CSortMenu::operator=` has two
    sites (CQstLogList ctor, CMenuQuestLog Init: out of line);
  - sites in functions that the linker later dead-strips. A global function
    that nobody calls still makes the count 2 (`void dead(E* a, E* b)
    { *a = *b; }` turns the ctor's `tbl[i] = buf` into
    `bl __as__1EFRC1E`). An *uncalled inline* function body does not count.
- The element copy inside an implicit array `operator=` is a call site of the
  element's `operator=`. This replaces the earlier note "calls the element
  operator= only if it was already generated by a direct use": the direct use
  is simply the second site.

**Rule B: per caller, inlining is all or nothing against a size budget.**

- Four assignments `s = S(0); w1 = W1(0); w2 = W2(0); w3 = W3(0);` in one
  function, each `W` with n int members. With n <= 92 all four are inlined.
  With n >= 93 none is, not even the 3-member `S`; all four become weak
  out-of-line functions in first-use order. One assignment alone flips at
  332 members, two at 153 each. Explicit `inline` functions called from the
  same function are dropped with them (`small()`/`big()` test).
- The caller's own code does not count (adding 400 stores to the caller
  changes nothing). Budget and flips are the same at `-O4,s` and `-O4,p`.
- Nested functions are judged inside the out-of-line copy. Once
  `CItemBoxLine::operator=` is out of line, its body applies rules A and B again
  on its own. Example: `CItemBoxPage` is copied twice in it, so it stays
  `ShopBuy_CopyData` = `__as__12CItemBoxPageFRC12CItemBoxPage`.

**Applied to the open cases**

- `CMenuItemExchange::Init` (rule B). Retail calls all four copies out of line:
  `ItemEx_CopyBgTex/CopyTitle/CopyLine/CopyGrid` are `__as__6CBgTexFRC6CBgTex`,
  `__as__11CTitleAHelpFRC11CTitleAHelp`, `__as__12CItemBoxLineFRC12CItemBoxLine`
  and `__as__12CItemBoxGridFRC12CItemBoxGrid`, in that first-use order. The cause
  is CItemBoxGrid's 0x638-byte copy, which puts `Init` over the budget.
  - Proof, in a scratch copy of the real TU:
    - Write the four lines as real assignments and give the grid a stand-in
      class with >= 200 int members. The output has all four weak `__as__`
      functions directly after `Init`: CBgTex 0x64 and CTitleAHelp 0x9C, both
      equal to retail. `Init` is 0x1B0; retail is 0x1BC, and the stand-in
      ctor takes three fewer arguments, which is three `li` = 0xC.
    - With <= 100 members everything is inlined, which is what the repo's
      CItemBoxGrid gives today: its copy is 0x44 bytes because of the
      `CibgSkip4` placeholders, so `Init` grows to 0x654.
  - CMenuShopBuy / CMenuCollepedia / CMenuKizunaTalkList have no huge member,
    stay under the budget and inline their copies.
  - CMenuItemExchange stays in its hand form until CItemBoxGrid has a real
    `CItemBoxGrid(u8, u16, u32, u8)` ctor and its full member layout.
- `CMenuKizunaTalkList::Init`: `mKizunaTalkList = CKizunaTalkList(0);`
  (one site, under the budget, inlined) replaces the raw `tempList` block.
  The unit stays 14/14 with extab MATCH.
- `QstInfo::operator=` is implicit (no user declaration).
  - CMenuQstCnt (-O4,s, many sites in Refresh/Sort): out of line, weak after
    Refresh, by rule A.
  - CMenuQuestLog (-O4,s, one site): inlined.
  - CQstLogList (-O4,s): retail calls it out of line in the ctor, so the
    original TU had a second `QstInfo` assignment. No live function shows
    one, so it was in code that was dead-stripped at link. The
    decomp keeps a minimal unreferenced `QstLogList_CopyQstInfo` (link-dead,
    excluded by the linked-view gates) and the ctor matches. The unit's extab
    is now the retail size (0x208; it was 0x220 while the TU called a declared
    but hidden `operator=`, which is not known to be nothrow). 44 byte diffs
    remain. `QstDataInline.hpp` (body hidden from one TU) is gone.
  - The same evidence pattern explains the weak `__dt__7QstDataFv` in retail
    CMenuQstCnt. No live code references it, and it sits right after the QstData
    ctor's weak functions, so a dead-stripped user sat between the ctor and
    `Refresh`. Not reproduced: its shape is unknown.
- Diagnostic: a weak copy function with only one live call site in a `-O4,s`
  unit means a second site exists, either inside another generated function
  or in dead-stripped code. In a `-O4,p` unit, or with one site, an
  out-of-line copy means rule B: look for a very large sibling inline in the
  same caller.

## CMCCrystalBox member classes (makecrystal, 2026-11)

- Weak inline emission order: retail order ParamTable ctor, Param ctor, Param::set, ParamTable dtor, SelTable ctor, SelTable dtor is reproduced exactly only when these are in-class inline members (first-use order under `-ipa file -inline auto`). Confirms they were real inline members.
- `CMCCrystalBoxParam::set(const&)` (not by value): const& lets MWCC schedule all loads before stores (retail); by-value interleaves lhz/sth. Fields must be u16 (retail uses lhz, not lha).
- Implicit `operator=` of a class whose element type has an inline `set` (no user operator=) gives the retail bitwise word-pair copy loop (`mParamTable = CMCCrystalParamTable();`).
- `CMCCrystalSelTable::getSelectEntry` retail indexes `mItems[mOrder[mTop - 1]]`.
- Unresolved conflict: `CMCCrystalData::~CMCCrystalData` is emitted out-of-line in code_80213488 (retail 0x80215388) yet the retail CMCCrystalBox dtor inlines it (DESTROYMEMBER names it, no call). Inline dtor -> CMCCrystalBox dtor 100% but code_80213488 extab mismatch (10/11); out-of-line -> code_80213488 11/11 but CMCCrystalBox dtor 54% (extra bl, 0xE4 vs 0xD8). Kept out-of-line. Probably a different TU-local visibility (e.g. dtor defined inline in a header code_80213488 forces out via a pointer/`delete`).
- Unresolved: decomp CMCCrystalBox ctor extab carries actions for the +0x2D6/+0x290 members that retail lacks (retail has none after the scrollbar); `throw()` specs did not change it.

## CSaveLoad / CMapSel / COption real classes (2026-11)

- `-ipa file` inlines callees that are defined *later* in the TU. Helpers that retail calls with `bl` need `__declspec(noinline)` or to be defined in retail text order before their callers.
- An empty out-of-line dtor in the TU (`CSLCur::~CSLCur() {}`, `CCur19::~CCur19() {}`) is inlined into the owner dtor (retail `addic.` null check + base dtor) and still emitted as a global symbol. This explains the stripped `__dt__8028xxxx` / `__dt__8029BF18` names next to the owner.
- Ctor stack slots: named block locals are allocated first, top-down, and compiler temporaries go below them. Mixing `{ X t(..); m = t; }` with `m = X(..)` in one function reorders the slots. Retail CSaveLoad ctor uses three named-local blocks (slots 0x80/0x44/0x08).
- Implicit `operator=` on an owner (`mMapSel = CMapSel();`, `mFade = CFade();`) inlines under `-inline auto`. Retail CMenuMapSelect::Init calls the weak `__as__7CMapSelFRC7CMapSel` / `__as__5CFadeFRC5CFade` out of line; `#pragma dont_inline on` around Init reproduces it exactly (Init 0x130, both weak copies at their retail sizes and order).
- CMenuSave / CMenuOption inline the owner `operator=` but call `__as__17UnkClass_8045F564FRC17UnkClass_8045F564` (and `InfoCfCopySysWin` / `MenuShopSellCopyCursor`) out of line. The monolib header defines the UnkClass `operator=` inline, CSysWin declares none, and CBaseCur declares none, so the decomp inlines those copies. This is unresolved while those headers are read-only.
- `u8 a[3]` copied by an implicit `operator=` is emitted as a halfword plus a byte.
- `(arr - 1)[index] = v` gives retail's `add` operand order for a 1-based index (CSLData::onSlotRead).
- CMapSel ctor: the map-id loop counter is `u8` (retail `clrlwi` + `cmplwi 28`). Retail also has the loop rotated and no jump-table range check; not reproduced (ctor 37%).

## CEquipChange / CEquipItemBox real classes (2026-11)

- CEIBCur has a 1-slot vtable (`[RTTI, 0, initLayout]`): no virtual dtor, no base list. Its empty dtor `CEIBCur::~CEIBCur() {}`, defined out of line before the owner, is auto-inlined into `~CEquipItemBox` (no call in retail) but still emitted for the ctor's DESTROYMEMBER +0x44. `~CEIBPageCur` stays a `bl`, so it needs `__declspec(noinline)`.
- The `mGrid = CEquipItemGrid();` temp in the retail CEquipItemBox ctor has no dtor call, yet DESTROYMEMBER +0x37E names a weak dtor. An in-class `~CEquipItemGrid() {}` gives both, and the ctor matches 100%. The `lbl_eu_806649E0 = 0` store sits between the grid copy and the `CItemBlock_setFlag120EC` calls.
- Retail `PartyStateWin_CopySlotRec` (0x34) is byte-identical to the weak implicit `__as__7CEIBCurFRC7CEIBCur` our build emits. It is the linker-kept CEIBCur `operator=` (first copy in CPartyStateWin). Likewise `MenuShopSellCopyCursor` is the CBaseCur-family copy.
- Unresolved: in the CEquipChange ctor's `mEquipItemBox = CEquipItemBox()`, the implicit box `operator=` calls `__as__7CEIBCur` out of line for both cursors but inlines the CCur18 copy (+0x74). Retail calls `MenuShopSellCopyCursor` there. This is the same CBaseCur header issue as CMenuSave above. The ctor is 49.9% only because of this +0x24-byte shift, plus one `lwz r5` scheduling slot later in the CItemBoxPage tail.
- Converting `grid->member` bodies to members: watch parameters and locals that shadow members (`u16 idx` vs member `idx`, `u32 cat`, a local `count`). The text rewrite silently changes semantics. In retail, three "box" helpers (getEIBProgress, hasEIBSlotFlag, getEIBNameKey) receive the grid as `this`, so they are CEquipItemGrid members.
- Box getters that retail CEquipChange tests unmasked (getEIBOpenFlag, eibWindowsReady, takeEIBAction, getEIBSelCat, ...) return `int`. The callee is unchanged (`lbz; blr`).

## Shared copy helpers are implicit operator=; rule A reads the end-of-TU size state (2026-11-18)

- `MenuShopSellCopyCursor` (0x34, CMenuShopSell, after Init) is the weak
  implicit `CBaseCur::operator=` (`__as__8CBaseCurFRC8CBaseCur`). CBaseCur needs
  no user declaration: assigning any `CCurNN` temporary (`mCur07 = CCur07(acc);`)
  inlines the trivial derived `operator=` and calls the base one. In a -O4,s TU
  with several cursor assignments the base copy has several sites, so rule A
  puts it out of line. CMCCrystalBox / CEquipChange / CItemBoxLine /
  CMCGetItemBox now use real assignments; CEquipChange ctor 95.4% -> 99.3%,
  CMenuOption Init 100%. CMenuShopSell's own Init is still an empty stub, so
  that TU no longer emits the copy (it shows as missing there).
- `InfoCfCopySysWin` (0xA4, CMenuItem) is the weak implicit
  `CSysWin::operator=` (`__as__7CSysWinFRC7CSysWin`): the decomp's implicit
  copy matches it byte for byte (load-all/store-all, mMemRegion inlined).
- `PartyStateWin_CopySlotRec` is the weak implicit `CEIBCur::operator=`. It is
  emitted after its first use in the CEquipChange copy (CPartyStateWin), and the
  CEquipItemBox ctor calls it as `mCur44 = temp; mPageCur = temp;`.
- **Rule A is applied at the end of the TU, using the `optimize_for_size` state
  in force there, not the state at the caller.** CSaveLoad was built -O4,p with
  `#pragma optimize_for_size on` regions. Its ctor (inside such a region)
  inlined both `CSysWin` copies. Switching the unit to `-O4,s` while the file
  still ended in `optimize_for_size off` (the cf::CfAward tail) still inlined
  them. With the unit at `-O4,s` and the CfAward tail wrapped in
  `push / optimize_for_size off / pop`, so that the TU ends in size mode, the
  two copies become calls (2 sites), the single `CScrollBar` copy stays inline,
  and the ctor is 100%. Diagnostic: a unit that needs many
  `optimize_for_size on` pragmas is a -O4,s unit, and its speed-optimised part is
  probably a second source file that shares the split (here cf::CfAward).
- The `-O4,s` setting alone does not cover a TU whose source copies are still
  hand-written stand-ins of generated `operator=` bodies (CPartyStateWin,
  CMenuItemExchange's `ItemEx_CopyLine`). In retail, rule B keeps the nested
  copies out of line inside those big generated functions. Those stand-ins are
  wrapped in `#pragma dont_inline on`, with a comment, until the owner classes
  are real.
- CMenuMapSelectSC Init: retail calls `__as__7CSysWin` twice, for the two
  CSysWin members of CFloorMap at +0xB8/+0xF4. The hand copy had dropped the
  second one. With both written, the copy has 2 sites and goes out of line.
- `~CMCCrystalData` conflict resolved: code_80213488 (CMCCrystalData members,
  0x802152E0..0x80215710) is the head of the CMCCrystalBox TU. The text,
  extab, extabindex and sdata2 ranges are contiguous with CMCCrystalBox, and
  CMCCrystalBox.cpp already held the rest of CMCCrystalData. Merged the split
  (us/eu/jp). The out-of-line empty dtor is now inlined into `~CMCCrystalBox`
  (same TU, `-ipa file`) and still emitted as a global. All 11 former
  code_80213488 functions still match, and `__dt__13CMCCrystalBoxFv` is 100%.

## cf actor hierarchy: MI vtable layout, key function, thunks (2026-11-18)
- **MI vtable layout (verified with test compiles).** MWCC emits one
  `[RTTI, offset-to-top, slots...]` group per base, in base order. Every group's
  RTTI word points at the most-derived class. A derived class appends the
  virtuals it declares, in declaration order, to the group of the **last**
  base. An override gets a new tail slot only when no offset-0 slot already
  exists for that name. Secondary-base slots point at `@N@name` this-adjust
  thunks (`subi r3,r3,N; b name`, 8 bytes).
  `cf::CfObjectActor : CActorParam(+0), CAIAction(+0x3380), CfObjectMove(+0x3E9C)`
  reproduces the retail 0x5D4 group structure exactly. The Actor tail
  (0x5A0..0x5D0) is: dtor, hasActorScale, clearStatusPair, flushStatusPair,
  takeDamageValue, getMoveHeadAngle, getAdjustedFacing, readActionScale,
  sharesMoveFlags, pushRefreshValue, setTargetC4Arg, getActionSrcId,
  clearActionSrcId.
- **Key function.** The vtable is emitted in the TU that defines the first
  virtual declared in the class that is neither inline nor pure. RTTI is weak in
  .sdata and the base list is a local `@N` in .data. Making
  `CBattleState::CBattleState_getOwner` and `CActorParam::CObjectParam_getParamPtr`
  real out-of-line members moved both vtables back into their own TUs:
  `__vt__Q22cf12CBattleState` (ex `lbl_eu_8052E9B0`; the split now gives
  CBattleState .data 0x8052E9B0..EA40) and `__vt__Q22cf11CActorParam` (ex
  `lbl_eu_80531870`). Both are byte-identical.
- **Inline virtuals and thunks** are emitted weakly in every TU that emits a
  vtable needing them, and the linker keeps the first copy. Retail keeps the
  Actor thunks and the inline Actor/CActorState bodies in CfObjectEne.cpp. The
  `@16028@` dtor thunk is the exception: it closes CfObjectActor.cpp.
  `@N@` names cannot be spelled in C, so while hand vtables remain
  (code_800C17DC Pc/Ene tables, CActorParam/Ene hand thunks), these symbols are
  named `thunk_8_<mangled>` / `thunk_3E9C_<mangled>`. Hand thunks that call
  same-TU members need `#pragma dont_inline on`, because MWCC otherwise inlines
  the target into the thunk.
- **Override return types follow the base.** `CfObject_pushRefreshValue` is
  `void*` (it returns `this`). The `mr r3,r31` epilogue in
  `CfObjectMove::CfObject_pushRefreshValue` disappears if it is declared `void`.
  `CBattleState_callOwnerObject` is `void*`: the base returns 0 and the Actor
  override (`blr` only) returns `this`.
- **Blocker: extern "C" declarations named like compiler symbols.** These cause
  10322 "illegal name overloading" as soon as the class emits the same symbol.
  For example, `plugin/pluginEve.cpp` has `extern u32 __RTTI__Q22cf11CActorState[]`,
  so an inline `CActorState::setObjStateBit3` cannot be emitted there.

## cf leaf classes (Ene / Pc / Npc): emission order, RTTI externs, member dtors (2026-11-18)

Verified while turning `CfObjectEne`, `CfObjectPc` and `CfObjectNpc` into real
classes (compiler vtable, RTTI and `@16028@` thunks).

- **Declaration order does not steer thunk or inline-body order.** Swapping
  the in-class order of `CBattleState_getOwner` / `callOwnerObject` in the
  derived class changed nothing. Functions that need a thunk are emitted before
  the other vtable-referenced inlines, and thunks close the TU. Retail has the
  two owner getters and their `@8@` thunks in the opposite order to ours (same
  bytes, different slot-to-address mapping); the cause is still open.
- **A virtual call to an inline virtual emits its weak body right after the
  caller.** The remaining vtable-referenced inlines follow at TU end, per
  class, in reverse definition order.
- **Member destructors need real member classes.** With a real member
  (`CAIActionRing` holding `CAIActionSlotQueue`) the inlined dtor addresses the
  member from the base pointer register (`addic. r3,r0,4`); a cast of
  `&this->field` folds to `this+const` and does not match. A user-declared
  inline dtor that gets inlined into an emitted dtor is still emitted
  out-of-line as a weak function (`~CAIActionSlotQueue`); an implicit one is
  emitted and dead-stripped.
- **`static_cast<Base*>(p)` as a function argument gets a null guard; a member
  call through `p` does not** (`cmpwi; beq; addi 0x3E9C` versus a bare
  `addi`/`lwzu`). Retail has no guard at these sites, so
  `self->CfObjectMove_isEffectSlotUsed(...)` or a qualified
  `CfObjectMove::CfObjectMove_attachEffectSlot(...)` is the source shape, not a
  helper returning the base pointer. The guard also appears for
  `static_cast<Base*>(this)` passed to a free function.
- **An extern named like an RTTI object can break a TU that generates that
  RTTI.** In `CfObjectEff.cpp` (emits the `CfObjectEff` vtable and RTTI,
  direct base `CfObject`), `extern "C" const void* __RTTI__Q22cf8CfObject;`
  gives 10322 at the point the compiler first needs the RTTI (end of
  namespace, or a `dynamic_cast`), whether the extern comes before or after
  the class definition. `CfObjectEne.cpp` saw the same extern and compiled, so
  the trigger is narrower than "the TU generates this RTTI"; it was not
  isolated further. Keep such externs out of shared headers
  (`CTaskGameEff.hpp` reached `CfObjectEff.cpp` through `harness_catalog.hpp`).
  Where the TU has the class, write the real `dynamic_cast` instead: in
  `CfObjectEff.cpp` `dynamic_cast<cf::CfObjectEff*>(cfObject)` produces the
  same bytes as the hand `__dynamic_cast(obj, 0, &dstRtti, &srcRtti, 0)` call
  (argument 3 is the destination type, argument 4 the static source type).
- **An extern "C" function named like a member of the TU's own class** also
  gives 10322 once the class emits its vtable, so a hand vtable cannot live in
  the TU that defines those members as real members.
- **`-RTTI off` on a unit removes the RTTI word, the base list and the name
  string**, which shifts `@stringBase0` by the name length; byte-identical
  functions then fail the reloc-site check. `CfObjectNpc.cpp` still carries
  that flag in `configure.py`; compiled with RTTI on, its vtable is 139/139
  words identical to retail.
- **String pool order is first use across the whole TU.** Replacing hand
  offsets into a label (`&lbl[0x19A]`) with literals makes each offset depend
  on every earlier function referencing the same strings. In CfObjectEne the
  pool is 0x11 short until the unmatched functions reference `"elem_tol_dir"`
  and `"str"`, so `initEnemyBdatParams` differs by one `addi` immediate.
- **File-scope `char* p = "literal"`**: a literal of 8 bytes or less goes to
  the `.sdata2` pool, a longer one to `.rodata` ahead of the RTTI name and the
  pooled strings.
- **Open: inline `1..0x18` range helper.** Retail tests the battle-manager
  byte with two `cmplwi` (`< 1`, `> 0x18`) around `li r0,0` / `li r0,1`. Every
  inline `bool` helper shape tried (`&&`, nested `if`, `else if` ladder, local
  copy of the byte) folds to `addi -1; clrlwi; cmplwi 0x17`; only two separate
  `if (...) goto` tests written directly in the caller keep both compares.
  `CfObjectPc::CActorParam_UnkVirtualFunc88` stays at 95% on this.

## Parameter-type conversions at call sites: u8/u32 are passed raw, bool/int are converted (2026-11-18)

Verified with stand-alone test TUs compiled with the project flags (`Wii/1.1`,
`-O4,s -inline auto -ipa file`). Writing `c->m8(v)` / `c->mb(v)` / `c->mu(v)` /
`c->mi(v)` for the same argument expression shows which argument types cost
instructions at the *caller*:

- `u8 -> u8` and `u8 -> u32`/`int`: **no instruction** (the value is passed in
  the register as-is; MWCC does not zero-extend for a wider parameter).
- `u8 -> bool` or `int -> bool`: `addic rX,rA,-1; subfe rX,rX,rA` (two
  instructions, normalising to 0/1).
- `bool -> u8`: `clrlwi rX,rX,24`. `bool -> u32`/`int`: no instruction.

Consequences for "flag" helpers (`setPaneVisible`, `CBaseCur::SetVisible`,
`CCur11::ShowTwoPanes`, `CSubCur::ShowTwoSubPanes`, `CEquipChange::ShowSubPanes`):

- A forwarding chain only stays conversion-free when every hop has the *same*
  declared type. `CEquipChange::ShowSubPanes` is 8 bytes in retail (`addi r3,
  r3,0x80; b ShowTwoSubPanes`), i.e. it forwards r4 untouched, so its parameter
  and the callee's must both be `bool` (the split annotation said `FUc`; the
  emitted body proves `Fb`). With `u8` the caller gains the 2-instruction
  `addic/subfe` pair.
- A local passed to a bool parameter must be declared `bool` (`int flag;
  ... ShowTwoPanes(flag)` adds `addic/subfe`; `bool flag` does not).
- `setPaneVisible(Pane*, bool)`'s body (`pane->SetVisible(visible)`, nw4r's
  `mFlag = visible` on a `u8` member) contains `rlwinm r0,r4,0,24,31` — that is
  the bool->u8 store conversion, so the helper's own parameter really is
  `bool`; do not "fix" it to `u8`/`u32` to silence a caller-side `addic`.
- A return value consumed by `!= 0`/`if (f())` must not be declared `u8` unless
  the caller really masks: with `u8 BothSubPanesOn()` every caller gained
  `rlwinm r0,r3,0,24,31` before its `cmpi`; declaring it `int` reproduces the
  retail `cmpi cr0,0,r3,0` (the callee returns 0/1 in r3 either way).

Also: a split symbol's `...Fv` annotation can be wrong. `CItemBoxLine::
ResetCursorB8` was annotated `Fv` but retail's 8-byte body is `addi r3,r3,0xB8;
b ShowTwoSubPanes`, which forwards r4 — a no-parameter body would need `li r4,
<const>` first (0xC bytes). Changing the parameter to `bool` and renaming the
symbol to `...Fb` turned it into a 100% match.

## RVL_SDK bte bta_dm_act / WUD — Wii-era BTE struct layouts and event ids (bta_dm_act 14→48 of 56 FULL_MATCH)
- Symptom: BTE callbacks matched instruction-for-instruction except for struct
  field offsets/immediates (e.g. `addi r4,r31,3` vs `,1`, `li r0,516` vs `,517`),
  or sized 8-0x100 bytes off.
- Cause: the SDK headers in the tree are AOSP-flavoured; the retail Wii-era
  BTE stack differs in a handful of layouts. All of these are *retail-proven*
  (reloc + offset evidence), so fix the local view, not the body:
  - `BD_NAME_LEN` is 0xf8: `tBTA_DM_AUTH_CMPL` = bd_addr@0, bd_name@6 (0xf8),
    key_present@0xfe, key@0xff, key_type@0x10f (0x110 total, the frame says so).
    `tBTA_DM_PIN_REQ`/`tBTA_DM_AUTHORIZE` put dev_class/service at 0xfe.
  - `tBTA_DM_DISC_RES`: bd_addr@0, bd_name@6 (0xf8), services@0x100 (4-aligned
    after the name => 2 pad bytes), result@0x104.
  - `tBTA_DM_CFG` field order is dev_class, **policy_settings@4,
    page_timeout@6, link_timeout@8** (the caller's three `lhz` offsets prove it).
  - `tBTA_DM_PEER_DEVICE` strides 11 bytes (`mulli r28,r0,11`): bd_addr@0,
    in_use@6, policy@7 (+3 unknown).
  - `tBTM_RSSI_RESULTS` / `tBTM_LINK_QUALITY_RESULTS` are status, hci_status,
    value@2, rem_bda@3 (i.e. the value comes *before* the address).
  - `tBTM_REMOTE_DEV_NAME` is status@0, length@2, remote_bd_name@4 — every
    remote-name callback takes that pointer (not `(bd_addr, dc, name)`).
  - `tBTM_CB.page_timeout` sits at +0x64c (declare the extern with 0x64c of
    leading padding, or the load loses its displacement).
  - `tBTA_DM_SEARCH` = union{inq_res(0x0c), inq_cmpl(1), disc_res(0x108)}; a
    function that keeps one costs a 0x108-byte frame slot.
- Signatures that change codegen (all retail-proven):
  - `BTM_ReadRemoteDeviceName` returns `int`; call sites compare
    `(UINT8)BTM_ReadRemoteDeviceName(...) == BTM_CMD_STARTED` (the `rlwinm
    r0,r3,0,24,31` before `cmpli 1` disappears if you declare it `u8`).
  - `BTM_GetNumAclLinks` returns `UINT16` (`rlwinm r0,r3,0,16,31`).
  - `L2CA_SetIdleTimeoutByBdAddr`/`L2CA_SetIdleTimeout` timeout params are
    `UINT16` (`0xFFFF` is materialised as `subi/rlwinm`, not `li -1`).
  - `BT_BD_ANY` is `const BD_ADDR` (an array): `extern const unsigned char
